title_as_printed: TABLE II. Apparent molal volumes of aliphatic hydrocarbons in water solution.
pressure_note: not stated: solutions saturated with the gas at a 'desired pressure' read on a manometer (gas partial pressure = final minus initial pressure; value not printed); the property is an infinite-dilution-type apparent molal volume, approximately at atmospheric pressure

T.note: constant per block, set by the T label rows (group_rows T.constant)

P.note: not stated; gas partial pressure near atmospheric

value.what: apparent molal volume psi of the dissolved hydrocarbon (cc per mole), stated by the author to be identical with the partial molal volume in these very dilute solutions; from Eq. (1) with the measured specific gravity and the concentration y

y.what: hydrocarbon concentration in g/cc, calculated from the measured gas partial pressure with Henry's law and the solubility data of Claussen and Polglase (1952), not analysed directly

one_minus_d_over_d0.what: 1 - specific gravity of the solution relative to air-free conductivity water at the same T (measured, communicating-tube copper-block apparatus)

skip_rows.reason: gas label rows and temperature label rows

extra_unmapped: Av. rows (authors' averages, the footnote-a values excluded)
conversion_needs: psi rows with note 'psi cc:a' (rows 5 and 27) were omitted by the author from the averages; builder may flag them
notes: Printed layout: per gas, side-by-side temperature sub-blocks (methane: 16.8, 23.0, 29.1 C in one band, then 35.1 C in a second band; ethane and propane: 16.9, 23.0, 29.1 C). Stacked: gas label row, then for each temperature a label row 'T=..C', its data rows, and its 'Av.=' row (left block first). The ethane 16.9 C block has a single row and no printed average. Row indices 0-based after the header. Precision for the aliphatics is lower than for benzene (author: concentration data less accurate). Gases ch4, c2h6, c3h8 set by group_rows.
